video_title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
gist: Zeno Rocha explains how Resend (4.3M users, 120K paid customers, SDK downloads >2x Send Grid's) won developers from neglected incumbents like Twilio's Send Grid via DX, trust-by-default onboarding and automated abuse controls, and is now moving off Amazon SES to own its sending infrastructure. A major theme is agents as distribution: Claude Code recommends Resend 60%+ of the time, its MCP doubles monthly, and machine-readable pages (markdown, llms.txt, FAQs) shape AI recommendations.

themes.theme: Resend traction vs. legacy email incumbents

insights.claim: Resend powers 4.3 million users, crossed 120,000 paid customers, and counts Warner Brothers and HBO among customers; users grew from 1 million in December to roughly 4 million.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: A developer-first email API is scaling ~4x in under a year — evidence the transactional email category is being re-platformed by newer entrants.
insights.quote: So, Recent now is powering 4.3 million users as of this morning.

insights.claim: Resend's SDK downloads surpassed Send Grid's earlier this year and are now more than double, though Send Grid still sends far more total email due to big enterprise customers.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Developer adoption (SDK downloads) is a leading indicator; volume share still favors incumbents, so watch for enterprise migration as the lagging signal.
insights.quote: And then earlier this year we crossed the number of uh downloads from S grid and I was like that's insane and now we're more than double.

insights.claim: The investment thesis for Resend was simple: Mailchimp and Postmark had exited and Send Grid sat neglected inside Twilio, leaving no one serving the developer persona in a massive email market.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Incumbent consolidation into larger parents creates openings for focused challengers in 'boring' infrastructure categories.
insights.quote: Look, uh, Mailchimp has exited, Postmark has exited, Send Grid is under Twilio, who is doing this?

insights.claim: Rocha argues Twilio neglected the developer-focused products (Send Grid, SMS) that built it while pivoting its marketing toward 'customer AI', suggesting the incumbent is 'sleeping on' its core.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: A signal of potential share loss for Twilio's email/SMS developer franchise to specialized challengers.
insights.quote: I go past that 101 billboard and I see a customer AI or whatever, I'm pissed. I'm like, why? Like you neglected the thing that got you there.

insights.claim: Scale appears to confer limited advantage in email delivery: a ~100x-larger incumbent (Twilio, roughly a $13-15B company per the host) could not stop a better product from winning developers, and email/SMS are commodity-like with slim margins.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Low scale economies plus commoditization imply product/DX is the moat — and also cap pricing power across the sector.

insights.claim: Mailgun's founder told Rocha he sold quickly because 90% of R&D went to fighting abusers, calling email sending a terrible business.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Abuse-fighting cost is the hidden structural drag in email infrastructure; winners must automate trust & safety to preserve margins.
insights.quote: 90% of our R&D was just to fight abusers. So it was a it's a terrible business.

insights.claim: Resend is reaching $10M-scale enterprise customers without a traditional sales org, having only just hired its first account executive while staying ~50 people and remote.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Product-led growth carried Resend far; turning on enterprise sales is the next lever for ARR expansion.

insights.claim: Rocha believes selling to enterprise means building a different product, not just adding SSO, SCIM and audit logs to the pricing page.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Dev-tool companies moving upmarket face real product investment, not checkbox features — watch for execution risk in that transition.

insights.claim: Gmail throttles bulk sends and watches early engagement, so senders should place the most engaged recipients at the front of the queue, space batches, and balance across providers and IP pools.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Deliverability is an operational/infrastructure moat, not a commodity API — a key reason challengers can differentiate.

insights.claim: Mailbox providers reward steadily increasing send volume and penalize bursty send-then-silence patterns, because the latter mimics abusers; good email practice is the inverse of phishing behavior.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Explains why naive in-house or cheap senders suffer deliverability issues and why managed platforms can charge a premium.
insights.quote: you need to do exactly what an abuser wouldn't do. It's the opposite of that.

insights.claim: A Japanese crime gang recently tried to onboard about 20,000 domains across registrars onto Resend, illustrating the scale of fraud that email platforms must screen (domain age, live website, lookalike domains).
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Abuse pressure is industrial-scale; trust & safety tooling is core cost and capability for any email platform.
insights.quote: there was a Japanese gang that recently came. they they brought like maybe 20,000 domains at recent

insights.claim: Resend trusts users by default (no human pre-approval like legacy providers) and then blocks quickly on bounce/complaint signals, finding most problems are misuse rather than abuse.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Frictionless onboarding drives adoption, viable only with fast automated enforcement — a differentiator versus gatekeeping incumbents.

insights.claim: Auto-generating a plain-text version of every HTML email increased Resend's deliverability 'a ton' because spam filters can read content directly.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: A concrete product-level deliverability gain that legacy players often don't bake in.

insights.claim: Open-rate tracking has become unreliable because Apple's privacy changes and AI summaries pre-load emails, pushing senders toward click tracking.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Email marketing analytics vendors relying on opens face a measurement problem; click and conversion metrics gain importance.

insights.claim: Rewriting tracked links to a shared provider domain is risky: one abusive customer can get that domain blacklisted for days or weeks, harming every customer (noisy-neighbor problem).
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Architecture choices around shared domains/IPs create systemic risk in email platforms.

insights.claim: Sender reputation has shifted from IP-based to domain-based, so best practice is separate subdomains for transactional vs. marketing streams; buying lookalike domains (e.g., an extra .com) looks like phishing.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Shifts control of reputation to the sender's domain strategy, reducing the moat of owning clean IPs alone.

insights.claim: At least ~60% of Resend's sent email goes to Gmail, followed by Outlook and Yahoo, with Apple significant and stricter because of auto-generated private relay addresses.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Gmail policy changes are the single biggest swing factor for the entire email-sending industry.

themes.theme: Moving down the stack off AWS SES

insights.claim: Resend started on Amazon SES but is now building its own sending infrastructure down to the metal — buying IP blocks, managing IP pools, and controlling throughput per mailbox provider — with an announcement coming soon.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Owning infra should improve gross margin, throughput and deliverability, and reduces dependency on AWS; a classic DX-layer-to-infra playbook.
insights.quote: So we are we're building the infrastructure and going like down to the metal now.

insights.claim: SES's hidden cost is the surrounding apparatus — SNS for events, CloudWatch for logs, SQS for queues, and custom webhooks — so the true footprint is much larger than the headline price (e.g., freeCodeCamp's ~$5,000/month for 5 million subscribers).
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Total cost of ownership comparisons favor managed platforms more than headline per-email pricing suggests.

insights.claim: Resend moved its sending path from Node.js/TypeScript to Go for performance, as AI coding makes language choice cheap.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: AI-assisted rewrites lower the cost of performance re-architecture, accelerating infra ownership for startups.
insights.quote: in the sending path we no longer use a JavaScript we have go there

insights.claim: Owning the infrastructure lets Resend surface far richer observability (whether email landed in inbox vs. promotions), addressing a long-standing blind spot in the email industry.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Observability could become a paid differentiator versus incumbents' opaque delivery.

insights.claim: Contact-based pricing in email marketing is breaking because AI companies such as Mistral add users so fast; Resend is working to fix that model.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Expect pricing-model disruption in email marketing (per-contact pricing at Mailchimp/Substack-style vendors) as AI-native customers scale.
insights.quote: the business model of contactbased pricing is kind of broken and we are realizing that and trying to fix that too.

themes.theme: Agents as the new distribution channel (MCP, CLI, AEO)

insights.claim: Claude Code recommends Resend 60%+ of the time for email, even when a user already has Cloudflare email configured — making AI-model recommendations a primary distribution channel for dev tools.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Being the default recommendation of coding agents is a winner-take-most distribution dynamic for developer infrastructure.

insights.claim: Resend's MCP server has grown at least 2x month over month, reaching about 1.2 million calls by the end of August, despite the narrative that MCP was dead in favor of CLIs.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Agent-driven usage is a fast-growing demand channel; tools without official MCPs risk losing selection.

insights.claim: Rocha now chooses B2B software based on whether the vendor offers an official MCP: he dropped Plausible for PostHog and picked Strava because they had first-party MCPs.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: First-party agent integrations are becoming a buying criterion — a churn risk for SaaS vendors lagging on MCP.
insights.quote: I need the owner of the software to own this piece of integration.

insights.claim: Resend's MCP has grown from ~20 tools to 80+, contrary to Cloudflare's minimal two-tool approach, and Rocha has not observed tool-count confusion in models anymore.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Design choices for agent interfaces are unsettled; full API coverage may win over minimalism.

insights.claim: Building a remote MCP forced Resend to rebuild its permissions model and OAuth, and getting into official lab connector stores required significant effort but matters for distribution.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Agent-readiness requires real auth/infra work — a barrier that favors API-first vendors.

insights.claim: Rocha observed (at least with Opus 4.5) a recency bias in model recommendations favoring newer tools with lots of organic discussion, which let Resend overcome incumbents' 10+ years of SEO.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: AEO resets incumbents' SEO advantage — a structural tailwind for new dev-tool entrants.

insights.claim: After an LLM wrongly called Resend's pricing obscure because it couldn't execute the JavaScript calculator, Resend published a markdown version of the pricing page and the model got the numbers right days later.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Machine-readable pages (llms.txt, markdown, FAQs) directly affect AI-driven competitive comparisons and win rates.

insights.claim: Resend's AEO playbook: FAQs on nearly every page, llms.txt and markdown versions of all docs and marketing pages, long-tail framework docs, and text versions of chart data; it pays for four AEO tracking subscriptions like Profound because none tells you what action to take.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: AEO tooling is still reporting-only — an opening for vendors that prescribe actions.

insights.claim: Competitors' comparison pages against Resend get recommended by models more than Resend's own migration pages, per Rocha.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Comparison content is a direct lever in AI recommendations.

insights.claim: Rocha says Reddit, Hacker News and Twitter matter less for distribution now, while the host runs an agentic 'CMO' loop with Ahrefs and DataForSEO tooling to experiment on AEO.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Marketing work is shifting to agent-run experimentation loops connected to analytics.

insights.claim: React Email served as Resend's open-source top-of-funnel ('our Next.js'), fixing template pain first and then funneling users to a platform to send.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Open-source wedge into a paid infrastructure product is a repeatable dev-tool GTM.
insights.quote: React email is our nextjs, right?

insights.claim: Domain Connect, an obscure 'OAuth for domains' protocol, removes DNS setup friction; Resend helped bring Vercel on board while GoDaddy charges a lot for it.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: DNS onboarding friction is the top support issue for new vibe-coding users; protocols that remove it boost conversion.

insights.claim: Vibe-coding users from Lovable, Bolt and v0 are a new audience that can't troubleshoot, making DNS setup the majority of Resend's support questions.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: AI app builders expand the market but raise support costs; automated onboarding is key to unit economics.

insights.claim: Resend hand-writes every SDK (including Java, Rust and .NET) rather than using generators like Stainless or Fern, caring even about languages with only a few hundred users.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Signals a craft-heavy DX strategy; also a quiet critique of auto-generated SDK vendors.

insights.claim: The host argues a Next.js mistake is that server components encourage binding data to pages so teams never build a public API; backends should be headless with the frontend as one client.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: API-first architecture becomes more valuable as agents become primary consumers of software.

insights.claim: Resend is launching programmatic inbox APIs (create many inboxes, read/star/label APIs) for agents, competing with shared-inbox products like Front and Missive.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Agent email inboxes are an emerging category (alongside AgentMail, Poke) to watch.

insights.claim: Resend's support policy required answering tickets only with a link to a docs article, building the knowledge base; scaling support remains a challenge as users quadrupled while keeping a free tier.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Free tiers plus docs-driven support are how PLG infra companies contain cost-to-serve.
insights.quote: you can only respond to a ticket with a link.

insights.claim: A YC partner told Rocha he cared too much about design; he chose to keep design as Resend's differentiator in a crowded market of products with poor design.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Design/taste can be a moat in commoditized infrastructure categories.

insights.claim: Rocha would rather run a $10M ARR company with a close relationship to his daughter than a $100M company without it, and is spending more time in Brazil.
insights.speaker: Zeno Rocha
insights.so_what: Founder priorities may shape growth pace and ambition; relevant for investors assessing trajectory.
insights.quote: I would rather live in that reality than live in a reality where we're hundred million dollar company and my daughter doesn't want to play with me.

insights.claim: The host argues Resend has achieved category dominance but not category creation, citing HubSpot's 'inbound marketing' as the model of a two-word category name.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Category creation lets a company own a whole market narrative; Resend's positioning is still 'next-gen Send Grid'.
